value: The mainstay of the region's reds, made on its own and as the base of Bordeaux style blends.
source_notes: James Suckling report: Cabernet Sauvignon is "the unabashed mainstay in Ningxia" among red varieties. Wine Folly: Ningxia "specializes in Bordeaux varieties, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Cabernet Gernischt", and Gernischt is often blended with Cabernet Sauvignon. SevenFifty Daily: Cabernet Sauvignon among the international reds that "continue to perform strongly" there.

value: Here it often shows herbal, medicinal notes and can taste green when not fully ripe.
source_notes: James Suckling report (Ningxia): many Cabernet Gernischt wines "underripe, smoky, green, and medicinal". SevenFifty Daily (Ningxia, quoting winemaker Christelle Chene): it imparts floral aromas "like hints of medicinal herbs". Wine Folly: Chinese wines of the Cabernet family often have a bell pepper (pyrazine) flavour. Two independent outlets agree on the medicinal herbal note; the green note rests on Suckling plus Wine Folly at country level.

value: A cross of Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache that has won wide favour here and suits the dry climate.
source_notes: SevenFifty Daily: Marselan, a cross of Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache, "is particularly well suited to its arid climate" (Ningxia). James Suckling report: Marselan "has gained immense success and popularity" and its freshness under heat is magnified in Ningxia.

value: In Ningxia it tends to give round, fleshy reds with plenty of fruit and soft tannins.
source_notes: James Suckling report (Ningxia): "round tannin, the wealth of fruit". SevenFifty Daily (Ningxia): producers let Marselan "express its hallmark fleshy mouthfeel".

value: One of the Bordeaux grapes the region specialises in, grown alongside Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Gernischt.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Ningxia "specializes in Bordeaux varieties, including Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, and Cabernet Gernischt". SevenFifty Daily: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah "continue to perform strongly" in Ningxia. James Suckling report also lists Merlot among Ningxia reds (planting share deliberately not used).

value: One of Yantai's main red grapes, grown alongside Cabernet Gernischt and Merlot despite the rainy summers.
source_notes: Wine Folly: in Yantai "you'll find plantings dedicated to Cabernet Gernisht, Merlot, and Cabernet Sauvignon"; Shandong climate maritime with monsoons and high rainfall. Decanter China (Yantai region authorities piece): Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Gernischt, Merlot among the usual varieties; summer rain and fewer sunshine hours the main challenge.

value: One of Yantai's main red grapes, grown alongside Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Gernischt despite the rainy summers.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Yantai plantings dedicated to Cabernet Gernischt, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon; maritime, monsoon climate. Decanter China: Merlot among the usual Yantai varieties; rainy summers the main challenge.

value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Syrah and Merlot, and bottled on its own under the Rift Valley label.
source_notes: Embassy of Ethiopia in Brussels: Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon chosen for the reds; lists "Rift Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2013". Winemag.co.za (David Bristow): reds made from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah. Jancis Robinson tasting listing for a Rift Valley Cabernet Sauvignon/Merlot (title only, paywalled). Lower tier sources, so weak.

value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon, and bottled on its own under the Rift Valley label.
source_notes: Embassy of Ethiopia in Brussels: Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon chosen for the reds; lists "Rift Valley Merlot 2013". Winemag.co.za: reds made from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah. Lower tier sources, so weak.

value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, and bottled on its own under the Rift Valley label.
source_notes: Embassy of Ethiopia in Brussels: Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon chosen for the reds. Winemag.co.za: reds made from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah. Jancis Robinson tasting listing "Rift Valley Syrah NV Ethiopia" (title only, paywalled). Lower tier sources, so weak.

value: The only white grape of the Castel estate near Ziway, grown beside its three red grapes.
source_notes: Embassy of Ethiopia in Brussels: "Chardonnay grapes were chosen for the white wines". How We Made It In Africa: Castel production "made up of cabernet sauvignon, merlot, syrah, and chardonnay". Winemag.co.za: whites led by Chardonnay. Lower tier sources, so weak.

value: One of the red grapes allowed by the appellation rules for its red, rosé and grey wines, and part of the blend of Château Roslane's premier cru red.
source_notes: Moroccan ministerial order 1957/98 on AOC Les Coteaux de l'Atlas, Article 2 (WIPO Lex text; FAOLEX scan is the same order, so one body): Cabernet Sauvignon listed for reds, rosés and greys. Viniou listing of Château Roslane 1er Cru Les Coteaux de l'Atlas: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah. Second source is a wine database listing, so weak.

value: One of the red grapes allowed by the appellation rules for its red, rosé and grey wines, and part of the blend of Château Roslane's premier cru red.
source_notes: Moroccan order 1957/98, Article 2 (WIPO Lex; FAOLEX scan of same order): Merlot listed for reds, rosés and greys. Viniou listing of Château Roslane 1er Cru: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah. Weak second source. Blend proportions deliberately not stated, see flags.csv.

value: One of the red grapes allowed by the appellation rules for its red, rosé and grey wines, and part of the blend of Château Roslane's premier cru red.
source_notes: Moroccan order 1957/98, Article 2 (WIPO Lex; FAOLEX scan of same order): Syrah listed for reds, rosés and greys. Viniou listing of Château Roslane 1er Cru: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah. Weak second source.

value: Allowed for the appellation's red and rosé wines, it is grown here on hills cooled by winds off the Atlantic, notably by Domaine des Ouled Thaleb.
source_notes: Moroccan order 1956/98 (FAOLEX scan, OCR read): for the Zemmour, Zenata and Sahel appellations among others, Syrah is listed among grapes for red or rosé wines. Skurnik (importer of Thalvin and Graillot Syrocco): Zenata has "cool winds blowing off the Atlantic"; Syrocco made by Alain Graillot and the Thalvin winery in Zenata. The Wine Society: Syrah du Maroc Tandem, Graillot and Thalvin (Ouled Thaleb). Importer and merchant sources, so weak.

value: Plantings are growing in Hokkaido, whose cool climate the GI rules describe as suited to it, and Yoichi has become its best known area.
source_notes: GI Hokkaido product specification (NTA interim translation): Hokkaido is classed Region I and "suitable for Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Germany varieties". GuildSomm (Yasha Lysenko): "plantings of Pinot Noir are expanding" in Hokkaido, and "a new generation of producers is crafting impressive Pinot Noirs". Nippon.com: warming has made Yoichi "better suited for Pinot Noir cultivation".

value: Here it is light in colour and body, with high, clear acidity.
source_notes: GI Hokkaido specification: red wines "light cherry red", taste "moderate or light", with "clear acidity and mild astringency" (all Hokkaido reds, not Pinot only). Nippon.com: Yoichi Pinot Noir growers emphasise "the Yoichi-characteristic high acidity". Weak because the spec describes reds in general.

value: Planted here as a cold hardy red grape able to face Hokkaido's harsh winters, alongside Kerner.
source_notes: GuildSomm: in Hokkaido, "cold-hardy varieties, such as Kerner and Zweigelt". Nippon.com (Yoichi): growers "tried growing varietals suited to colder climates, such as Seibel, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner, Zweigelt, and Pinot Noir".

value: One of the cold climate German grapes that Hokkaido growers turned to, and allowed under the GI Hokkaido rules.
source_notes: Nippon.com: Yoichi growers tried "varietals suited to colder climates, such as Seibel, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner". GI Hokkaido specification: Muller Thurgau is in the list of permitted vinifera, and Hokkaido is "suitable for ... Germany varieties".

value: In Hokkaido it is crisp and light, with a fresh citrus scent and clear acidity.
source_notes: GI Hokkaido specification: whites have fruity aromas "of a bright flower, green apple or orange", "rich acidity", and are "fruity and light" (all Hokkaido whites). Hokkaido Government Ishikari Subprefecture page on a Kerner from Kimura Farm: "a refreshing citrus aroma". Weak: spec is general and the second is one wine.

value: With Merlot, it is the grape Nagano producers have gathered around, and the GI Nagano rules place the two together in their first group of European grapes.
source_notes: GI Nagano product specification: "Group A: Merlot, Chardonnay" (vinifera). GuildSomm: in Nagano "there is some consolidation around Chardonnay and Merlot" (share figure deliberately not used).

value: With Chardonnay, it is the grape Nagano producers have gathered around, and the Kikyogahara area of Shiojiri made its name with it.
source_notes: GuildSomm: consolidation around Chardonnay and Merlot in Nagano. GI Nagano specification: Group A Merlot and Chardonnay; a Kikyogahara Merlot won a gold award, "making Kikyogahara famous for the place of producing the Merlot grape". Château Mercian (producer) makes its top cuvées from Kikyogahara Merlot. Weak because the Kikyogahara claim rests on the spec plus a producer.

value: The main grape of Osaka wine, a table grape made into still and sparkling wines, dry and sweet, and the GI rules allow it to be picked early for a fresher style.
source_notes: GI Osaka product specification: "Osaka wines are made mainly from Delaware and other table grape varieties"; early harvested Delaware allowed at 12.0% juice sugar; effervescent and sweet wines included. Wineanorak (Jamie Goode, Katashimo Winery visit): a sparkling Delaware with "a touch of sweetness" and a still Osaka Delaware. Weak: second source is a personal wine blog.

value: Here it gives light, fresh wines with a lemony, citrus edge, most marked when the grapes are picked early.
source_notes: GI Osaka specification: Delaware wines have "a refreshing, fresh aroma"; "a refreshing flavor like a citrus is emphasized when grapes are harvested early". Wineanorak: Osaka Delaware palate "light and fresh with nice direct lemony fruit". Weak: blog source.

value: Long the prefecture's main table grape, it is also made into wine from dry to sweet, and Takahata is one of its centres.
source_notes: GI Yamagata specification: Delaware planting made Yamagata a major grape area and once covered most of its grape land; young winemakers work on wines "mainly made from labrusca varieties such as Delaware"; wines dry and sweet. Tohoku Tourism Promotion Organization: Takahata Town has the largest shipment of Delaware grapes for wine in Japan (ranking not used). Visit Yamagata (Omotenashi Yamagata): Delaware used in Takahata wines. Tourism sources, so weak.

value: One of the European grapes established in Yamagata through hedge training and rain covers, and a key grape for Takahata's wines.
source_notes: GI Yamagata specification: "particularly Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay were established there through the introduction of the hedging-style growing method, ... vinyl tents for protection from rain". Tohoku Tourism: Takahata Town has the largest shipment of Chardonnay grapes for wine in Japan. Visit Yamagata: Chardonnay used in Takahata wines. Tourism sources, so weak.

value: Here it makes light, delicate and understated whites, with quiet orchard fruit rather than strong aroma.
source_notes: GuildSomm (Yamanashi): Koshu "largely been associated with weightless, delicate wines", naturally only about 11 to 12% alcohol, "delicate classic Koshu aromas". The Wine Society (Andrew Jefford in Japan): "an understated white", "light and precise", "fugitive orchard-fruit charm".
